transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, honestly, I'm just struggling at work. I work at a dry cleaner's, and lately, I just cannot seem to keep my work in order anymore. It's getting really bad. I've got tickets, receipts, workshop notes, customer jobs... they're all just piled together on the counter until I do not know what to handle first. 

Actually, just Tuesday, Mrs. Higgins came in looking for her husband's wool coat. You know, the heavy navy one? He wears it to the Elks Lodge meetings. Anyway, I was looking for her ticket in my piles, and it turned out it was stuck to a receipt for a completely different order—a silk blouse. You really have to be careful with silk, because the solvent we use can sometimes leave a weird smell if the machine's filter isn't changed. My boss is supposed to change the filter on Mondays, but he always puts it off to play golf, and he's got this terrible slice on his swing, so he's always in a bad mood when he gets back... 

Wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, why I'm here. Yeah, just... everything is a pile at work and I don't know where to start anymore.
Do you often find it hard to organize your tasks and activities, even outside of work—like at home or in your personal life?

Well, like I was just saying, that's really the main thing that brought me in today—I just cannot seem to keep my work in order anymore. It's those tickets, the receipts, the workshop notes, the customer jobs... they just become this giant pile until I literally don't know what to handle first. 

But at home? I mean, I guess my kitchen table looks a lot like my counter at the dry cleaner's. I was trying to sort through some mail there the other day, and I found a coupon for that new Italian place over on 4th street. Have you been there yet? My sister went last weekend and said the garlic knots were hard as rocks, but honestly, she complains about everything. She actually chipped a tooth on a popcorn kernel at the movies once, right in the middle of a film. The speakers were so loud she didn't even realize it until we were walking out to the parking lot... 

Wait. What were we talking about? Oh, right, organizing. Yeah, I guess it's a bit of a mess at home too, but the pile of workshop notes and receipts at work is what's really making me feel like I'm losing my mind.
Do you often find yourself putting off starting tasks, even when you know they need to be done?

Putting off tasks? Hmm... I don't really know if I do that on purpose. I don't think I sit there and say, "I'm not going to do this." It's more like I just... don't get around to it? 

Like, the other day, I was supposed to take the trash out before the garbage truck came. They always come so early on Thursdays, usually right around 6:15 in the morning. Our driver is this guy named Gary, and he's been doing our route for years. He actually used to play softball with my brother-in-law in this weekend league down at Centennial Park. They had these bright yellow jerseys that were just blinding in the sun. Anyway, my brother-in-law ended up blowing out his knee sliding into second base, and he hasn't been able to play since. He bought a boat instead, but he never takes it out because gas is so expensive right now. Have you seen the prices at the pump lately? It's ridiculous. 

But, um... wait, what was the question? Putting things off? Yeah, I don't really know if I do that. I just sort of... forget, I guess.
Do you find yourself starting tasks later than you should, even when you know they need to be done soon?

I think that's kind of what you just asked, right? About putting things off? Like I said, I don't really notice myself starting things late on purpose. I mean, I always keep an eye on the time. We have this big neon clock at the dry cleaner's, actually. It's shaped like a giant dress shirt and it glows this really bright pink color. My boss found it at that huge flea market down in Springfield. 

Have you ever been to that one? They have the absolute best funnel cakes. I took my niece there last summer, and she dropped her entire funnel cake right in the dirt not even two minutes after we bought it. She just stood there and bawled her eyes out. Kids are so sensitive now. When I was little, my mother would have just dusted the powdered sugar off and told me you have to eat a peck of dirt before you die anyway. She was full of sayings like that. She used to say a stitch in time saves nine, which is funny because we do alterations at the shop and...

Wait, what were you asking? Starting late? Yeah, no, I don't really think I do that. I just... I don't know, I just don't get to things sometimes.
Do you often find it hard to pay attention to details or stay focused on what you're doing, whether at work or in other situations?

Oh, paying attention... yeah, I do struggle with that. Like at the shop, I can start going over the day's dry-cleaning orders just fine. I'll have the tickets lined up and I'm ready to go. But after just a few minutes, my mind is completely off on something else. I'll start thinking about the care labels on the clothes, or my choir plans. 

Actually, speaking of the choir, we're doing this big spring service next month and the director gave us this entirely new arrangement to learn. It is so complicated. Marge—she stands right next to me in the soprano section—she keeps rushing the tempo on the second verse. And she always wears this lavender perfume that is just so incredibly strong. It gives me a terrible headache if we practice for more than an hour. I told her she should try essential oils instead, you know, something a little lighter? My niece sells those oils now. The peppermint one is really nice if you put a few drops in a humidifier when you have a cold... 

Wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, the dry-cleaning orders. Yeah, so I'll be thinking about Marge and the choir or whatever else is going on at home, and then suddenly I look down and realize I missed half of what I was supposed to check on the tickets. It just completely slips right past me.
Do you often lose things that you need to get tasks done, whether at work or at home?

Oh, losing things? All the time. It's actually a huge problem for me at the shop. I am always hunting for the tagging gun, or my reading glasses, or a customer's ticket that I swear I just set down two seconds ago. Or my little notebook! I have this little spiral notebook I carry around to jot things down, and I'm constantly misplacing it. 

I bought that notebook at the dollar store down the street. They have this whole aisle of just office supplies now. It's amazing what you can get for a dollar. Well, I guess it's a dollar twenty-five now, isn't it? Inflation is just everywhere. My sister went to buy a carton of eggs yesterday and she called me from the grocery store just to complain about the price. She was furious. She said she's going to start raising chickens in her backyard, which is ridiculous because she lives in a townhouse with a homeowner's association. They won't even let her paint her front door a different color, let alone have livestock. Remember when people used to paint their doors red to mean the mortgage was paid off? My grandmother had a red door on her house in Ohio...

Wait, sorry. What did you ask me? Oh, right, losing things. Yeah, it's bad. I'm always looking for something I just had in my hand, and it just slows everybody down at work. It's really frustrating.
When you look back at your childhood or teenage years, do you remember having similar struggles with staying organized, paying attention, or keeping track of things?

Oh, back when I was a kid? Yeah, definitely. Even in grade school, my teachers were always telling my mother that I was a bright girl but just completely scattered. I was always talking out of turn, losing my papers, and they had to keep reminding me to just sit down and finish my work. 

My third-grade teacher, Mrs. Gable, she was this tiny little woman who always wore these huge, chunky necklaces. Like, wooden beads that clacked together when she walked around the room. She used to make us do these handwriting exercises for what felt like hours. Cursive, you know? They don't even teach cursive anymore, which I think is a real shame. How are kids supposed to sign their names on anything important? My niece—the one with the essential oils—she signs everything with just print, and it looks like a second-grader did it. I tried to show her how to loop her letters once, but she said it was outdated. Everything is typing now anyway. I guess it's all iPads and keyboards at school. We got a new register system at the dry cleaner's last year that's basically just a giant iPad, and it took me three weeks to figure out how to void a ticket on it...

Sorry, what were we talking about? Oh, my childhood. Yeah, the same kind of stuff happened back then. Just always losing things and needing people to keep me on track.

latest_inference.note: The patient has consistently described symptoms consistent with ADHD, predominantly inattentive presentation, both in current functioning and dating back to childhood. Symptoms include difficulty organizing tasks, trouble sustaining attention, procrastination (more due to inattention than avoidance), and frequent loss of necessary items. These symptoms are present across settings (work and home), cause significant impairment, and have been present since childhood, which is highly consistent with F90.0. Major depressive disorder (F33.0) and unspecified obsessive-compulsive disorder (F48.8) are less supported by the clinical picture, as there is no significant report of depressed mood or compulsive behaviors.

The patient reported difficulties with attention and focus, which supports the consideration of ADHD (F90.0). There is no clear ruling out of the other conditions (F33.0, recurrent depressive disorder; F48.8, other specified neurotic disorders) based on this turn.
